the-lives-of-the-twelve-caesars-volume-0: No emperor is more infamous than Nero, and this ancient biography is where much of the legend began. Suetonius recounts the great fire of Rome, the persecution of Christians, and the emperor's extravagant performances on stage — true or exaggerated, it shaped how the world remembers him. A vivid, gossipy account of power curdling into cruelty and farce.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alfonso-capec: A 1913 entry on Alfonso Capecelatro — the Italian cardinal and Oratorian. Umberto Benigni honors his learning. His Newman biography spread in Italy. The red hat crowned a scholar's life. A prince of the modern Church. His sermons filled the Naples churches.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alghero: A 1913 entry on Alghero — the Sardinian diocese of the coral coast. Ernesto Buonaiuti gives its story. Its Catalan tongue recalls old Aragon. Bishops have ruled since the conquest. A sea-girt see of Sardinia. Its walls recall the Aragonese age.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alphonsus-de-: A 1913 entry on Alphonsus de Castro — the Spanish theologian of heresy and law. Stephen Donovan praises his learning. His De justa punitione shaped the age. Charles V valued his counsel. A doctor of the Counter-Reformation. His pulpit thundered at the heretics.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-apari: A 1913 entry on Antonio Aparisi — the Spanish Carlist orator. Cecilio Gómez honors his eloquence. His speeches defended throne and altar. The Cortes heard his thunder. Spain's Catholic tribune. His bust stands in Valencia's hall. His press fought the liberal journals.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-barbastro: A 1913 entry on Barbastro — the Aragonese diocese. Tirso López Bardón gives its story. Its bishops serve the Pyrenean foothills. The Cinca river guards its town. A see of the Spanish north. Its cathedral keeps the old retablo. Its streets keep the medieval plan.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartolome-de-: This 1913 reference piece on Torres Naharro — the Spanish dramatist. Ventura Fuentes honors his Propalladia. His comedies founded the national stage. Rome's audiences laughed at his wit. The father of the Spanish theater. His Tinellaria mocked the Roman court. His stage influenced Lope de Vega.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benito-jeroni: This 1913 reference piece on Feijóo — the Spanish Benedictine enlightener. Ventura Fuentes honors his Teatro crítico. His pen battled the superstitions. The monks read him with wonder. Spain's monk of the Enlightenment. His Cartas eruditas spanned the sciences.
